burghers: citizens of the Boer republics, especially the Dutch-descended men entitled to vote
itlanders: foreigners, mostly British, living in the Transvaal without full political rights
itlander: a single foreigner, usually British, living in the Transvaal without voting rights
suzerainty: overlordship; a stronger state's right to control a weaker one's foreign affairs
uzerain: an overlord; a state holding authority over a weaker, dependent state
casus belli: an event serving as a justification for going to war
onvention: a formal agreement or treaty between governments, such as the 1881 settlement
arroo: the Karroo, a dry, semi-desert plateau in southern Africa
esert: a dry, barren region with little rain, vegetation, or population
franchise: the legal right to vote in public elections
suffrage: the right to vote in political elections
plateau: a broad, high, fairly flat area of land
tableland: an elevated stretch of level or gently rolling ground
malarious: infested with malaria; unhealthy because of mosquito-borne fever
malarial: caused by, or relating to, the disease malaria
salubrity: healthfulness; the wholesomeness of a climate or place
water-shed: a ridge of high ground dividing one river system from another
tributaries: smaller streams or rivers that flow into a larger river
parched: dried out thoroughly by heat, sun, or lack of rain
ultimatum: a final demand whose refusal would lead to war or other action
annexation: the formal taking of a territory into another state's control
rotectorate: a territory protected and partly controlled by a stronger foreign power
predominance: dominance; superior influence or control over others
preponderance: greater weight, number, or influence in one party's favour
vexatious: causing annoyance or trouble, especially without good reason
disaffection: discontent with, and loss of loyalty towards, the ruling authority
hostility: open enmity or aggressive opposition between parties
concession: something yielded or granted, such as a special right or privilege
expedition: an organised journey made for a particular purpose, such as exploration
hypothesis: an unproven explanation or assumption put forward for testing
eland: a large African antelope with spiral horns
ivory: the hard white tusk material of elephants, valued for carving
herbaceous: having soft, non-woody stems, as with herbs and most flowering plants
prickly-pear: a cactus with flat, spiny pads and edible fruit
mimosas: flowering trees or shrubs of the acacia family
kinship: close family relationship, or a close similarity in character
munitions: military weapons, ammunition, and other war supplies
diplomacy: the conduct of relations between states through negotiation and agreement
arbitration: settlement of a dispute by a neutral third party whose decision is binding
despatch: an official message or report sent from one government or officer to another
mischief: harm or trouble, often caused deliberately or by reckless behaviour
forbearance: patient self-restraint in not acting against provocation or wrong
obscure: little known, unimportant, or not easily understood
legislature: the body of elected people who make and pass the laws
judiciary: the system of courts and judges that interprets and applies the law
scrub: low, stunted, dense bushes and brushwood covering poor land
tariff: a tax imposed by a government on imported or exported goods
partisans: committed supporters of a party, cause, or leader, often uncritical
salient: most noticeable or important; standing out clearly from the rest
municipal: relating to the local government of a town or city
ascend: go or climb upward to a higher level or point
impartial: treating all sides fairly, without favouring either party
dispensation: a special exemption or arrangement granted from a general rule
